sections.skill: Strategy: fill the most constrained cell first
sections.relationship: Students guess letters and get stuck. Looking for a row, column or cell with only one possibility turns the grid into a chain of forced steps.
sections.author_note: Students guess letters and get stuck. Looking for a row, column or cell with only one possibility turns the grid into a chain of forced steps.

lesson.title: Fill the most constrained cell first
text: For each empty cell, list the letters its row and column have not used yet.
A cell with only one possible letter is forced: fill it in.
Also look along a row: if a letter can go in only one cell of that row, it goes there.
Repeat. Each new letter removes options from other cells.

example.title: Worked example (a different grid)
prompt: Rule: each row and column of a 3 by 3 grid holds X, Y and Z once. Row 1 is X Y Z. Row 2 starts with Z.
steps: Row 2, column 2 cannot be Y (column) or Z (row), so it is X. Row 2 is Z X Y.
Row 3 gets the letter missing from each column: Y Z X.
